stances.summary: Early social media access delays student learning and development
stances.quote: Does Early Access to Social Media Harm Later Learning? New Evidence from Italy (by Marco Gui). Students who got social media accounts by age 12 progressed less than those who waited until age 14

stances.summary: Australian social media regulation policy is achieving positive results
stances.quote: Australia’s Social Media Policy Is Succeeding (by Ravi Iyer)

stances.summary: Tech companies harmed education; schools must reduce screen dependency
stances.quote: Why Did We Let Big Tech Take Over Education? (by Sophie Winkleman). Sophie Winkleman lays out the damage from the screen-based school day and shows how to roll it back.

stances.summary: Snapchat exposes minors to graphic violence and sexual predation
stances.quote: What Does a 13-Year-Old See on Snapchat in a Normal Week? (by Brooke Istook). Two new studies show that kids and teens frequently encounter graphic violence, sexual content, and adult strangers on the app.

stances.summary: Teen girl suicide rates rising globally, trend predates COVID-19
stances.quote: Teen Girls’ Suicide Rates Are Rising In Many Countries Around The World (by Jean M. Twenge). New analyses from Europe, Japan, and South Korea show increases that in many cases began before COVID.

stances.summary: Children overprotected offline, underprotected online from harms
stances.quote: The State of Childhood in the U.S. (by Lyman Stone). A new survey of U.S. parents by the Institute for Family Studies suggests that kids are still overprotected in the real world and underprotected online.

stances.summary: Community groups and outdoor play can restore healthier childhood
stances.quote: We Took Away the Phones — Now What?  (by Seth Kaplan). How rebuilding youth community groups can restore a play-based childhood.

stances.summary: Social media regulation essential for LGBTQ youth safety online
stances.quote: Don’t Let Big Tech Hide Behind a Rainbow Flag (by Lennon Torres). Lennon Torres on why social media regulation is a prerequisite for LGBTQ safety.

stances.summary: School phone use reduces academic performance and increases loneliness
stances.quote: Phones at School: Less Learning, More Loneliness (by Jean M. Twenge). A new analysis shows the twin impacts of the leisure use of devices during the school day: declines in test scores and increases in feelings of loneliness at school.

stances.summary: Skepticism toward technology necessary to protect human connection
stances.quote: Why You Should Be a Techno-Skeptic (by Jon Haidt). In his most urgent TED Talk yet, Jon Haidt reminds us that human connection is not optional.

stances.summary: Compelling evidence against social media will inform future litigation
stances.quote: The Case Against Social Media: Seven Lines of Evidence (by Jon Haidt). Your guide to the evidence that will help decide thousands of future court cases.

stances.summary: Indonesia's child protection regulation constrains harmful tech design
stances.quote: How Indonesia is Protecting 80 Million Children from Online Harm (by Anindito Aditomo). Their first-of-its-kind regulation cracks down on harmful design and incentivizes safer technology.
